title: Processing Activity Records template and audit notes
content:
Purpose
This file is a combined template and auditor-facing note set for maintaining Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) and associated evidence at Redwood Inference. It is intended for use by product teams, legal, and the security team when onboarding new features, vendors, or deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private).

Scope
- Applies to any processing of personal data by Redwood Inference or on behalf of customers where Redwood is a processor or controller.
- Includes product features, telemetry, customer-managed private deployments, and third-party integrations.
- Not a substitute for legal review; intended operational template to support DPAs and privacy-impact assessments.

How to use this template
- Fill each section with concise, factual statements. Use stable identifiers for processes (e.g., PA-2025-001).
- Link to evidence artifacts (logs, architecture diagrams, KMS policies) in the linked_artifacts field and in the evidence checklist.
- Keep the record updated with material changes and save a new version line at the bottom.

Record of Processing Activity (RoPA) template
1) Processing Activity ID: [PA-YYYY-NNN]
2) Feature / Service: [e.g., Hosted API inference telemetry v2]
3) Owner (product/legal/security): [Name, team]
4) Controller/Processor role: [Controller | Processor | Joint controller] and specify which entity (Redwood / customer / third party)
5) Purpose(s) of processing: [short bullet list - e.g., "model routing optimization; billing; fraud detection"]
6) Legal basis (for controller activities): [consent, contract, legitimate interest, legal obligation, public task] + brief justification
7) Categories of data processed: [e.g., customer account identifiers, request metadata, prompt text (if stored), model outputs, IP addresses]
8) Special categories (sensitive data): [Yes/No] + if Yes, describe safeguards and lawful basis
9) Data subjects: [end users, customer admins, device ids, employees]
10) Typical data flows / systems involved: [list: API gateway, inference cluster, KV cache, monitoring pipeline, metrics DB, analytics, KMS] + reference architecture diagram ID
11) Recipients / data sharing: [internal teams, sub processors, cloud provider regions, analytics vendors] + purpose for each recipient
12) Subprocessors (third parties engaged to process data): [name, role, country, contract reference, last security review date]
13) International transfers & safeguards: [countries, SCCs, BCRs, adequacy decisions, encryption-at-rest measures, customer-specific exceptions]
14) Retention policy: [retention period per category; triggers for deletion; retention justification]
15) Deletion / return procedure when contract ends: [steps, responsible team, timeline]
16) Security controls & safeguards: [access controls, encryption-in-transit, encryption-at-rest, KMS key policy id, MFA requirements, logging/monitoring]
17) Access rights and role mapping: [which teams can access what data; approval workflow; change control ticketing process]
18) Data provenance / source of data: [customer-supplied prompts, scraped corpora, partner feeds]
19) Data minimization notes: [what is minimised, sampling, prefixes trimmed, prompt redaction heuristics]
20) Data quality / accuracy procedures: [user correction flow, QA checks, automated validators]
21) Known legal or compliance constraints (e.g., export controls, CCPA opt-out specifics)
22) Relevant contractual clauses: [DPA clause ids, SLA clause ids, indemnities]
23) Evidence references (link to artifacts): [list of artifact IDs and brief description]

Auditor checklist (evidence to collect)
- R1: Completed RoPA entry exists for PA-ID above (Y/N) -> [evidence: confluence page id or doc location]
- R2: Architecture diagram aligned with entry (Y/N) -> [evidence: diagram file id; last updated date]
- R3: Subprocessor contracts on file and include required security/RoPA clauses (Y/N) -> [evidence: contract ids]
- R4: KMS key policies show separation of duties and rotation schedule (Y/N) -> [evidence: KMS policy id, rotation log sample]
- R5: Retention/secure deletion mechanism exists and has been tested (Y/N) -> [evidence: deletion run id, test report]
- R6: Access logs and IAM roles show only documented teams have access (Y/N) -> [evidence: IAM role list, sample log excerpts]
- R7: Data minimization and redaction logic is implemented in pipeline (Y/N) -> [evidence: PRs, unit tests, feature flags]
- R8: International transfers have documented legal basis/safeguards (Y/N) -> [evidence: SCCs or equivalent, transfer approval ticket]
- R9: Incident response playbook references this PA and has contact list (Y/N) -> [evidence: playbook id, runbook run id]
- R10: Privacy impact assessment (PIA) or risk memo produced for high-risk processing (Y/N/NA) -> [evidence: PIA id or risk memo link]

Evidence artefact guidance
- Use persistent IDs: confluence pages, git commit hashes, PR numbers, ticket ids. Avoid copy-paste of logs in docs; instead reference secure evidence store paths.
- For private deployments, attach customer-provided attestation or deployment report if they self-host components.
- Keep a red-team/QA test report for any model-eval that touches personal data.

Recommended contract language snippets (operational focus)
- Subprocessor notification: "Controller/Processor will publish an updated subprocessor list at least 30 days prior to onboarding; controller has the right to object in writing within 14 days."
- Retention authorisation: "Processor shall retain Personal Data only for the period necessary to fulfill the documented purposes or as required by law; upon expiry Processor will securely delete or return data per the deletion procedure."
- Evidence and audit access: "Processor shall provide reasonable documentation and audit evidence on request, including access to relevant logs under NDA and in accordance with security policies."

Notes for private/on-prem / VPC cases
- Customers operating a Private deployment may manage certain components themselves; the RoPA entry must clearly flag which components are customer-managed and which remain Redwood-managed.
- Evidence expectations differ: Redwood will provide design-level evidence and operational runbooks; the customer should provide on-site evidence (or remote attestation) for infrastructure logs and physical access controls.

Operational tips and red flags
- Red flags (escalate to legal/security): storage of full prompt text for >90 days, unrestricted internal access to raw model outputs containing PII, subprocessors in jurisdictions without adequate transfer safeguards without documented legal basis.
- Keep RoPA entries lightweight but authoritative: one paragraph per field is usually sufficient; link to deeper technical docs for complex flows.
- Automate parts of the RoPA where possible: populate systems inventory, KMS ids, and retention windows from service metadata.

Versioning and change log
- Version: 0.1-draft (this document)
- PA-ID: [PA-2024-078 sample]
- Change log example: 2024-09-18 created by Aisha Patel; 2025-04-02 updated subprocessors list (Luca Moreno); 2025-11-07 retention periods harmonized (Priya Shah)

Appendix: quick evidence mapping table
- Architecture diagram -> confluence:arch-PA-2024-078-v3
- Subprocessor contracts -> /vault/contracts/subprocessors/payments-co.pdf
- KMS policy -> kms-policy-id:rdw-kms-2024-03
- Deletion run -> ticket:OPS-3189

Endnotes
- Responsible teams should review this RoPA template annually or whenever a major product or legal change occurs.
- Questions or requests for legal wording should be routed to legal@redwood.ai with PA-ID in the subject.
